findings.field: meetings.fed.pricing.observable_proxy.implied_quarterly_average_rate; verification_note.known_limitations[2]; decision_brief.summary; decision_brief.what_is_priced.unavailable; decision_brief.changes_since_previous[1]; fed-boc-watcher/index.html Fed pricing-card label
findings.issue: ZQV26 is the October 30-Day Federal Funds futures contract, whose settlement is based on the average daily EFFR during its delivery month; it is not a quarterly-average contract. The payload calls its rate quarterly in several places, and the rendered Fed card displays '3.895% quarterly-average rate'. This conflicts with the candidate's own contract_horizon_caveat, which correctly calls it an October 30-day average. Neither contract-level average is a single-meeting probability.
findings.evidence: Headless Chrome --headless=new --dump-dom against the candidate rendered Fed card text '3.895% quarterly-average rate'. yahoo_ZQV26_CBT_daily.json has the Sep 28 close 96.105. CME's 30-Day Fed Funds rule language defines contract grade as 100 minus the arithmetic average of daily EFFR during the contract delivery month: https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/lookups/advisories/ser/SER-7594.pdf. Candidate meetings.fed.pricing.observable_proxy.contract_horizon_caveat itself says October 30-day average. By contrast, CRAU26 is the three-month CORRA contract and is appropriately described as quarterly.
findings.pnl_impact: Misstating the tenor can make a PM attribute a monthly average-rate exposure to a quarter or to the Oct 28 meeting, distorting hedge horizon and the interpretation of policy risk.
findings.instruction: Change the Fed-specific field description and renderer label to 'October monthly (30-day) average EFFR'; keep the separate CORRA proxy labeled quarterly. Correct every statement that calls both proxies quarterly, and do not convert either proxy into meeting odds.

findings.issue: The brief repeatedly says every priced contract is at its range midpoint and says 3.895% is within one basis point of the Fed midpoint. Neither statement is correct: the Fed range midpoint is 3.875%, so 3.895% is 2 bp above it; CRAU26's 2.375% quarterly-average rate is 12.5 bp above the BoC's 2.25% target, and the BoC target is not a target range. The headline and abstention rationale therefore contradict the quoted proxy values.
findings.evidence: Independent arithmetic command output: FED_MIDPOINT_DIFF_BP 2.0000000000000018; CORRA_ABOVE_TARGET_BP 12.5. Candidate values: ZQV26 close 96.105 -> 3.895%; CRAU26 bid/ask 97.62/97.625 -> approximately 2.375%. The raw Yahoo daily capture and TMX/MX CRAU26 row were inspected; the rendered card also shows these values. The candidate itself states these values in decision_brief.what_is_priced.fed and .boc.
findings.pnl_impact: This overstates the evidence for a neutral policy path and hides a measurable cross-quarter CORRA premium. A decision maker could dismiss priced rate drift or mis-size a position based on the false midpoint premise.
findings.instruction: Replace the blanket midpoint claim with the exact distinctions: ZQV26's October monthly average is 2 bp above the Fed target-range midpoint; CRAU26 implies roughly 2.375% average CORRA, 12.5 bp above the 2.25% policy target, across two decisions. Keep the no-trade rationale grounded in the unavailable single-meeting distributions and non-executable quote-side observation; correct all listed copies.
